subject: Post-call recap — batch sizing, latency SLOs, and topology options
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Patel <ravi@payload.ai>, Tim Rogers <tim.rogers@nebula.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — batch sizing, latency SLOs, and topology options

Hi Ravi / Tim — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned.

High-level pain & goals (what I heard):
- Payload is seeing tail latency spikes when concurrent inference requests exceed ~350 req/s for short prompts (~128 tokens).
- Average per-request throughput target: 300–500 req/s for the main inference endpoint (mixed prompt sizes), with 99th percentile latency target <= 250ms for interactive use.
- Cost pressure: want to keep steady-state GPU spend below $X/month (discussed offline) — interested in batching + KV cache + quantization to reduce token cost.
- Compliance: logs and audit trail retention for 13 months; may require VPC/private deployment down the road.

What we propose next (short list):
1) Tech deep-dive with your infra & engineering team to map real traffic patterns (histograms + concurrency). Bring any representative traces (you mentioned the latency CSV). — action: Ravi to send traces by EOD 4/30.
2) Redwood will draft 2 topology options: (A) Hosted dedicated pool with autoscale burst to meet peaks; (B) Private VPC pilot with KV caching and per-customer routing. We’ll include cost estimates for both.
3) SLO proposal: target P50/P90/P99 latency buckets and batch-sizing matrix for each prompt class. Karthik will propose an initial matrix; timeline below.
4) If topology A looks viable, follow-on POC: 2 week pilot with traffic mirror and nightly run of our throughput harness.

Immediate next steps & owners:
- Ravi: share payload_latency_trace.csv and any percentile SLAs you currently track (EOD 4/30) — acknowledged on call.
- Camila (me): coordinate deep-dive and schedule 60–90m technical session next week (suggest Tue/Wed in your timezone).
- Karthik + Markus: draft initial batch-sizing / SLO matrix and topology sketches by 5/2.
- Lauren: prepare MOP deck skeleton for procurement & risk (cc’d).

Attachments referenced: topology-diagram.png (sketch we drew on call), placeholder MOP deck.

Thanks — I’ll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive once I hear availability.

Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0114

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap — batch sizing, latency SLOs, and topology options — quick pre-read

Camila / team — quick pre-read ahead of the 10am deep-dive. High level estimates based on the 72h trace (assumptions noted):

Assumptions:
- Model: 7B decoder-only equivalent; baseline throughput measured on prod-gpu-a100-80GB.
- Token generation: average output tokens per request ~60.
- Two prompt classes: short (~90 tokens), long (~300 tokens).
- Target interactive SLO: P99 <= 250ms for short prompts; for long prompts P90 <= 650ms is acceptable (Payload has async fallback for >300 tokens).

Initial sizing & batch matrix (summary):
- To sustain 350 req/s with P99 <= 250ms (short prompts): need 6 x A100-80GB equivalent with continuous batching and KV hot-cache for common prefixes. Effective per-GPU steady req/s with batching ~60–70 req/s (depends on prompt mix).
- For peak 420 req/s (short prompt mix spike): autoscale to 8 GPUs (burst policy) to keep P99 under 300ms.
- Quantized 4-bit variant reduces memory footprint enabling denser packing but increases per-token latency ~10–15% — still useful for background workloads and for lowering cost for long, non-interactive batches.

Topology considerations:
- Hosted Dedicated (Option A): Dedicated GPU pool, Redwood-managed autoscaler, prefix KV cache at edge layer, and an L7 router that pins session-affinity for low-latency paths. Pros: fastest time-to-PoC, simpler runbook. Cons: SOC2 & procurement timeline.
- Private VPC (Option B): Customer VPC peered, private control plane, KMS integration for keys, and agent-based telemetry ingestion. Pros: meets strict data residency and security controls. Cons: longer onboarding + ops handoff required.

Open risks & asks for the call:
- Need more precise token distribution (we used 90/300 buckets) and request inter-arrival time distribution to refine batching window settings.
- Confirm whether the async fallback is acceptable for any P99 violations on long prompts.

Actionable next items (we’ll present these options + a cost delta table in the deep-dive):
- Karthik: full batch-latency curves for short/long profiles (deliverable 5/2).
- Markus: formal topology sketches with KMS/logging notes (deliverable 5/2).
- Camila: confirm legal/procurement contacts for SOC2 checklist.

See you all at 10.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
